# tests/fixtures/deproj/

## Purpose

Holds `.deproj` test fixtures consumed by
`tests/unit/deproj_round_trip_test.cpp` (Phase 8 cross-platform safety gate
per c142-C definitive gap inventory).

`.deproj` is the Decoda IDE project XML format used by the AAASeed runtime
(see `vendor/aaaseed-runtime/AAADecoda.deproj`). It is XML 1.0, UTF-8
encoded, and stores project metadata that the Lua editor (Decoda) reads.
The companion `.deuser` file holds the user-local working state (paths,
debug command line, SCC). Both are pure XML and therefore cross-platform
text by construction.

The AAASeed C++ engine itself persists scene state through XML-based save
files written by `c_app::save_to_file_add_ext()` and the
`aaa::file::save_type_io()` cascade declared in
`vendor/aaaseed-engine/Src/infrastructure/seedfile.{h,cpp}`. The
*defining* cross-platform safety property of these files is the rule
documented in `vendor/aaaseed-engine/CODE_STYLE.md` and reflected in
`vendor/aaaseed-engine/Src/image/pixel_format.cpp:243` :

> Persisted in .deproj files as string label, not numeric enum value.
> Existing labels are immutable (renaming = breaks old projects).

The round-trip test verifies the cross-platform safety claim of c142-C :
`.deproj` files are XML/UTF-8/ASCII-label and therefore safe to load,
re-save, and reload across Win/Mac/Linux without binary drift.

## Files

| File | Origin | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `minimal.deproj` | Generated at test runtime | Round-trip fixture (the test writes it on first run, then reloads it and re-saves a copy to compare). |

## How to regenerate

The fixture is generated by the test itself (Test 2 in
`deproj_round_trip_test.cpp`). To regenerate manually :

```bash
cmake --build out/cmake-build-v145 --target aaaseed_deproj_round_trip_tests
ctest --test-dir out/cmake-build-v145 -L deproj
```

The vendored sample lives outside this folder at
`vendor/aaaseed-runtime/AAADecoda.deproj` and is used by Test 1 (real
sample probe) -- do not copy it here ; the test reads it in place so the
fixture stays single-sourced from the runtime repo.

## Cross-platform safety contract (what the tests pin)

1. XML 1.0 declaration is present and UTF-8 encoded.
2. All bytes are 7-bit ASCII for the canonical empty form (no BOM, no
   non-ASCII).
3. No Windows-specific backslash path separators in the canonical empty
   form.
4. File size is plausible (> 0, < 10 MB) for a minimal project.
5. Round-trip preservation : re-emitting the parsed XML produces a file
   that re-parses to the same logical structure (semantic equivalence,
   not byte-identical -- whitespace and quote style may differ).
6. Enum string-label discipline : when an enum value appears in a
   `.deproj`, it is the string label (e.g. `"RGBA Fp32"`) not the
   underlying INT32 -- enforced by the engine's `c_param` save path,
   verified here as a property of the format.

## Why we do NOT link the engine loader

`seedfile.cpp` (1006 lines) transitively pulls in : truetype, bsp, fbx,
bdd_*, draw/*, media/video, render, stencil, fog, model, lights,
def_node, leveldata, ... -- a multi-hundred-TU cascade that crosses the
graphics-backend layer (Phase 3 not yet exited) and the layer subsystem
adapter fan-out (per the doctrine-limits note in MEMORY.md). Building a
hermetic Mac sub-lib via `std::` primitives (per the hermetic-Mac-sublibs
doctrine) sidesteps the cascade and lets us pin the cross-platform safety
contract today, before the full engine link is feasible.

When the full engine link lands (Phase 3 exit + layer port), a follow-up
integration test can promote these property checks to a real
`g_app->save_to_file()` invocation.
